title: fix(git): push can freeze the commit panel; timeout leaves GCM running
body:
Fix: a push can freeze the Git Changes commit panel for up to 5 minutes, and its timeout leaves Git Credential Manager (GCM) running. Found by the grug review of b17a049; the push now lives in src/git_history/push.rs (push, Target) and runs as commit::Write::Push through CommitPanel::start in src/git_history/commit.rs, started from the push dialog in src/git_history/changes.rs.

Two things are both called Job. commit::Job<T> is the panel's worker-reply handle (an mpsc receiver + cancel flag; its Drop only stores the flag). crate::job::Job in src/job.rs is a Win32 kill-on-close job object; see ai_oneshot.rs, integrate.rs, terminal.rs for how it is assigned right after spawn. Below, "job object" means the latter.

Problem (all verified on main):
- The push occupies CommitPanel.write, the single write slot. busy() then disables commit, add and Push for up to PUSH_TIMEOUT (300 s). There is no Cancel for a push (the only Cancel belongs to the AI draft).
- On timeout, git::write kills git.exe only (child.kill). GCM is a grandchild and survives with its sign-in window open, possibly behind foreman.
- GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 only stops console prompts; it does not stop the GCM window.
Note: Commit and Push already commits, frees the write slot, then opens the dialog; the push is a second write. Do not redo that. The remaining issue is that the push itself holds the slot.

Fix:
- git::write: add a cancel flag parameter and assign the child to a job object right after spawn. Timeout or cancel drops the job object (kill-on-close kills git.exe and everything it spawned). Only Write::Push passes a cancel flag and a timeout; Commit, Track, Rollback etc. pass None and are never killed (index.lock). While here: when there is no timeout and no cancel, call child.wait() instead of the 20 ms try_wait loop.
- The running push gets its own slot on CommitPanel (e.g. push: Option<commit::Job<Report>>), separate from write. While a push runs: commit and add stay enabled, the Push button and the push dialog are disabled (one push at a time), a spinner says "Pushing…" and a Cancel button sets the push's cancel flag. busy() keeps meaning "a write holds the index".
- The panel owns the push's cancel/job handle: closing the Changes window cancels a running push (safe: a killed push leaves nothing locked locally and the remote ref update is atomic). Document this; it differs from commits, which run to completion.
- Timed-out or cancelled push: the notice says the commit already landed and the push can be retried from Push… .
- When the push finishes, report wrote=true in Outcome so the status re-reads (the watch may already fire on refs/remotes; keep it correct either way).

Cleanups, all still present:
- CommitPanel's Drop spawns a thread just to drop a commit::Job whose Drop is one atomic store. Delete the thread; plain drop.
- Report and Notice overlap (Notice is Report minus committed/push). Collapse to one type or make Notice a view of Report.
- committing: Option<bool> exists only to choose spinner text. Replace with something that does not duplicate the write's state.
- Do NOT touch Outcome; it now has two fields (wrote, push) and is fine.

Tests (cargo test --target-dir target/agent):
- A hanging push is cancelled and its whole child tree is gone. Recipe: in a temp repo set core.sshCommand to a command that sleeps (e.g. powershell -NoProfile -Command Start-Sleep 600), add a remote with an ssh-style URL (host:repo), start Write::Push with a cancel flag, set the flag, then prove both git.exe and the sleeper died using crate::job::DeathWatch (cfg(test), src/job.rs). Mirror the pattern in ai_oneshot.rs tests.
- The same recipe with a short timeout returns GitError::TimedOut and the tree is gone.
- The panel can start a commit while a push is still running (push slot occupied, write slot free), and cannot start a second push.
- Existing push tests in commit.rs keep passing.

Docs: update docs/git-history.md (push dialog section and the "Commits and add are never killed" gotcha) to describe the separate push slot, Cancel, close-kills-push, and the job object. cargo fmt --check must pass.
